summary: A button that shows and hides a panel of content.

root.note: Stacks the trigger and the panel.

panel.note: The content that shows while open. The author marks it with data-part="panel".

caret.note: Optional: the icon in the trigger that the author marks with data-part="caret". It turns while open: a half turn, or a quarter toward the block end for a chevron-right, which is mirrored in right-to-left text.

keys.Enter, Space: On the trigger: show the panel, or hide it.

events.toggle: Dispatched, and bubbles, after the user shows or hides the panel. Not dispatched when a script changes open.

guidance.text: The trigger is the first element with the button role, or native button, that is not inside the panel. It may sit inside a heading. The panel gets an id only when it has none.

A ghost button as the trigger is the row: the heading that holds it and the button span the disclosure, at least a control tall, with the title at the start and a caret marked data-part="caret" at the end. A neutral or primary trigger keeps its own box.
